title: Spices and Dairy
story: The manager wants the healthy-stock list: only spice or dairy products with 20 to 100 units in stock.
goal: Show the names of products in the spice or dairy category with stock between 20 and 100 (inclusive).
starter:
SELECT name
FROM products
-- add a WHERE here
;

tests.label: Hidden check on other data
Hidden check on other data

hints: WHERE filters rows. IN (...) matches any value in a list, and BETWEEN a AND b includes both ends.
Join the two conditions with AND.
SELECT name FROM products WHERE category IN ('spice', 'dairy') AND stock BETWEEN 20 AND 100;
socratic: Which two things must be true for a row?
Compare the rows you got with the rows expected. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what does your query do?
solution: SELECT name FROM products WHERE category IN ('spice', 'dairy') AND stock BETWEEN 20 AND 100;
alt: SELECT name FROM products WHERE (category = 'spice' OR category = 'dairy') AND stock >= 20 AND stock <= 100;
